description:
Game markets Polymarket settled, as 0xinsider recorded them, oldest first: one row per market per settled state, the same object the market_settled webhook delivers as data. Use it to catch up on settlements after downtime, or as a pull alternative to the webhook: keep next_cursor and call again with it. Each row carries condition_id, settlement_id (one per market per settled state), event_slug, game_id, league, sports_market_type, outcomes (labels at their outcome index), copy_of_event_slug (always null here: a polyv2 copy of a game whose original has a moneyline is left out, as the webhook leaves it out of a league or type filter) and settlement: status observed, oracle_status resolved, settled true, payouts (micro-USDC per share per outcome index), result (outcome, or split for a 50-50), winning_outcome_index, was_disputed, resolved_at, expected_settlement_time, settlement_time_basis and observed_at, when 0xinsider first saw this state. A market can appear twice: once as a question row without payouts, then again with them. Unlike the webhook, a state first recorded more than 6 hours after its market resolved is listed, and so is a state naming the winner an earlier state of its market named (Polymarket's payouts row after the ConditionalTokens payout). Every plan.

Args:
  - since (string, required without cursor): RFC 3339 time; rows whose settlement.observed_at is at or after it
  - sports_market_type (string, optional): comma-separated provider market types, case-insensitive (moneyline, spreads, totals, a prop type). Default moneyline; * keeps every type, including markets with no stored type
  - league (string, optional): comma-separated leagues as the rows' league reports them, for example nba,epl; pga is PGA Tour golf
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20)
  - cursor (string, optional): opaque stl_v1_ cursor from next_cursor. It replaces since and keeps the filters it was issued for; filters sent with it must match them

Returns: data, has_more, next_cursor, complete_through and meta. complete_through trails now by two minutes: rows observed at or before it are served, so a row is never passed before it is recorded. has_more true means more rows up to complete_through remain: call again with next_cursor now. has_more false means the walk reached complete_through: keep next_cursor and call again later for what is recorded after it. next_cursor is always present. A page can hold fewer than limit rows, or none, while has_more is true: a read that has not filled its page stops after about 120 ms of scanning and resumes on the next page. A 503 read_model_warming means the first read did not answer in time: retry after Retry-After.
